title: Slam Shuffle
description: Shuffle a massive deck of cards using modular arithmetic and repeated function composition.
writeup:
## Approach

The key insight is that every shuffle operation is a linear function `f(x) = ax + b mod N` where x is a card's position. Reverse is `(-1)x + (-1)`, cut k is `x - k`, and deal with increment k is `kx`. All steps compose into a single linear function by multiplying/adding coefficients.

## Part 1

Compose all shuffle instructions into `f(x) = ax + b mod 10007`, then evaluate `f(2019)` to find where card 2019 ends up. Straightforward modular arithmetic.

## Part 2

The deck has ~119 trillion cards and the shuffle repeats ~101 trillion times. Direct simulation is impossible, but since `f(x) = ax + b` is linear, repeated application `f^k` can be computed via repeated squaring on the linear function coefficients — the same idea as modular exponentiation but for affine transforms.

The question asks which card is at position 2020, which means we need the inverse: `c = a_k^(-1) * (2020 - b_k) mod N`. Since N is prime, `a_k^(-1)` is computed via Fermat's little theorem: `a^(N-2) mod N`.
